newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended down on Thursday amid some impatience for clear signs of when an expected rate cut is going to come, dealers said.
But stocks were hoisted firmly off their day lows when favourable U.S. data gave another clear sign that inflationary pressure is easing across the Atlantic.
"What lifted us at the end was the U.S. numbers," one dealer said.
The U.S. July consumer price index came in line with expectations and spurred Wall Street shares into an early surge.
Local equites also immediately retraced some of their losses and the all-share index ended off 7.7 points to 7,530.3 as the industrials index dropped just 5.0 points to 9,238.1.
A rate cut is widely expected to come soon in South Africa, a reverse trend to the upward projections seen in most other major financial centres, but dealers said there was some edginess creeping in.
"If we don't get a signal soon, some guys might be keen to take profits before it happens," one dealer said.
Volumes on the day were healthy with 1.074 billion rands worth of stock changing hands. Gainers and losers were broadly balanced as 188 shares went up and 181 saw their prices come down.
The biggest of the losers was diamond giant De Beers which has taken a steep tumble since it posted disappointing half year results on Tuesday.
The share fell again in trade worth 101 million rand and ended off 150 cents to 153.00 rand. The fall has hit sister firm Anglo American which dropped 275 cents to 261.75 rand.
However, dealers were predicting a halt to the fall soon. "They must be getting close to a realistic value now," one trader said.
Elsewhere a drop in headline year earnings per share to 106.6 cents from 128.9 cents last time hit Unitrans stock which shed 90 cents to close at 19.60 rand.
In the financials sector half a million shares sold to a foriegn buyer in bank Nedcor saw the share drop 75 cents to finish at 95.75 rand.
Dealers said South African shares, which had on Wednesday reverted to their usual pattern of largely ignoring New York trends, were now watching U.S. stocks again for direction on Friday.
"The U.S. CPI figures were just too important," one dealer said, adding that the market was hoping for less volatility from Wall Street.

In the gold sector shares continued their gradual climb upwards on the back of stability in the gold price, but analysts are wary of serious resistance in the price of the yellow metal at the $330 an ounce level.
Bullion was last at $326 an the gold index gained 15.8 points to 1,041.9.
In futures near-dated industrial contracts traded mixed as the share market zig-zagged during the day.
The September all-share contract was last at 6,660/68 from 6,693 as the industrials contract was at 8,660/67 from 8,662. The golds contract was at 754/58 from 741.
